title: $1,700 Overnight. Not Your Requests.
caption:
I have one API key and it is pasted in four places.

OpenCode says someone reached a legacy system it was decommissioning on the night of Oct 16, and that provider keys saved in Console workspaces may have been exposed. It emailed 1.4% of Console users the next morning. They posted bills they never ran: $281 on OpenAI, $168 on Anthropic, one over $1,700 overnight. Google suspended some projects for activity consistent with hijacked resources.

The line that got me: deleting the key out of Console does not revoke it, and a Console budget cannot cap it either, because Console only meters what passes through its own gateway. Only the provider's dashboard kills a key. Keys added in the CLI or desktop app sit in SQLite on your machine and never reached OpenCode.

Anthropic revoked keys it believed were affected, Google blocked exposed Gemini keys, OpenAI says it refunded credits drawn in the attack. OpenCode calls it a large-scale distillation attack and says its own investigation stalled when the models it was using refused the requests.

Rotating mine tonight. How many keys do you have?

slides.title: CLI Keys Stayed Local
slides.sub: Terminal and desktop keys sit in SQLite on your machine. Only Console keys were at risk.

slides.title: Deleting Isn't Revoking
items: A provider key is a bearer credential.
Removing it from Console doesn't revoke it.
A Console budget can't cap it either.
Console only meters its own gateway.
Only the provider's dashboard kills a key.

slides.title: Projects Got Suspended
slides.sub: Google flagged activity consistent with hijacked resources. Projects went down too.

slides.title: Rotate, Then Split
items: New key first, then revoke the old one.
Check provider billing back to Oct 16.
Replace it in CI secrets and env files.
One key per tool, with a spend limit.
